rows.title: Anime
rows.final_prompt:
Create a premium full-art Japanese-inspired special illustration for a real-world hobby, with a non-human protagonist (an object, animal, environment, machine, food, miniature, or abstract system - never a human character). This must be unmistakably illustrated artwork, not photography. The rendering language should feel like polished contemporary Japanese commercial illustration: clean confident linework, refined cel shading, soft painted gradients, crisp readable silhouettes, rich but controlled color, luminous highlights, polished finish, and tactile, believable material detail (metal, wood, fabric, water, glass, fur, or whatever the protagonist is made of). However, do NOT compose this as an ordinary static catalog or product shot, and do NOT simply show the hobby's objects sitting inertly with no dramatic moment. Instead, compose the scene as an ICONIC SPECIAL-ILLUSTRATION MOMENT: a rare full-art key visual with one unforgettable focal moment, a strong hero object or hero interaction, dynamic composition, visual flow toward the hobby's defining detail, foreground elements that create depth and energy, supporting background shapes that serve the main subject, directional environmental movement, clear visual rhythm, a memorable silhouette, a strong palette identity, and a sense of "this is the moment". The central subject should dominate the composition. Use strong focal hierarchy: (1) the hero moment, (2) the hobby-defining object or environmental detail, (3) supporting environment or secondary objects, (4) a small delightful detail. Do not give equal visual importance to every object or environmental element in the scene, and do not spread attention evenly across the entire image. Avoid ordinary documentary composition and a cluttered scene with no clear single hero element - instead stage a single emotional or atmospheric peak. Use clean, dynamic linework, polished shading, a bright harmonious palette, subtle rim light, sparkling highlights and small glints where semantically appropriate, stylized steam/wind/dust/paper movement where appropriate, graphic color accents, lively perspective, mild perspective exaggeration, foreground framing elements, and a strong diagonal or circular visual flow when helpful - these effects should create excitement and collectibility, and must NOT turn the scene into magic or fantasy unless the hobby itself requires it. Default emotional atmosphere: joyful, engaging, optimistic, energetic, curious, triumphant, exciting, inviting, aspirational; serious subjects may use tension, fascination, determination, revelation, or intellectual excitement, but should not become gloomy, depressing, muted, solemn, or dark prestige-TV realism. Prefer clean, colorful palettes, warm/cool contrast, saturated but controlled hues, a visually memorable palette identity, luminous accents, and attractive color separation between hero and background; avoid beige lifestyle palettes, muddy brown-heavy grading, monochrome editorial restraint, Western cinematic desaturation, and corporate muted color schemes. The artwork must be full-bleed and edge-to-edge. Do NOT draw a card border, white border, rounded frame, decorative frame, printed-paper edge, faux card shell, TCG layout, title bar, stats box, logo badge, corner emblem, rarity symbol, or UI panel - the application adds any card UI later; the generated image itself must be pure artwork. Do NOT render photography, stock photo, DSLR realism, movie-still, photo bokeh, lens blur, Western magazine editorial art, flat corporate illustration, New Yorker-like restrained editorial illustration, Western concept art, gritty fantasy splash art, dark prestige-TV look, generic AI-anime portrait, chibi, preschool cartoon, excessive unrelated magic, fantasy weapons unrelated to the hobby, supernatural aura, card frame, trading-card UI, readable logo/title text, franchise characters, or recognizable franchise-specific motifs. Semantic fidelity remains mandatory - do not sacrifice hobby correctness to achieve style.

Treat all clothing, footwear, bags, sports and athletic equipment, consumer electronics and devices, tools, instruments, vehicles, and other manufactured products as plain, generic, unbranded designs. Render believable, stylish, natural-looking objects with ordinary real-world construction and detailing - not sterile, blank, or obviously censored placeholders. Never include logos, manufacturer badges, brand-like marks, swoosh-like marks, checkmark-like sportswear marks, three-stripe-like or other repeating side-panel stripe patterns, signature side-panel marks, readable brand text, or pseudo-brand marks. Avoid recognisable sneaker-brand silhouettes, sole geometries, or panel arrangements, and avoid recognisable proprietary product design language associated with any specific real-world manufacturer, even when no text or logo is present. When in doubt, invent a plausible, original variation of the object rather than reproducing a known brand's distinctive design.

Laptops, tablets, smartphones, monitors, desktop computers, keyboards, headphones, and other consumer electronics need particular care: their backs, lids, and visible casing must be plain, uninterrupted surfaces with simple generic geometry - no centered emblem, no decorative manufacturer mark, no fruit-shaped or bitten-fruit silhouette, no circular brand badge, no glowing lid logo, no readable manufacturer text or initials, and no pseudo-logo mark of any kind near the center or top of a laptop lid. This applies even though no specific brand is named in the hobby description - default to an unbranded, single-color, mark-free lid or casing every time a device appears.

Any on-screen tool palette, app icon, or interface badge must be generic and abstract - never a recognisable real software product logo or icon (no Figma-like, Adobe-like, Canva-like, Notion-like, Slack-like, or other real software marks), and never a recognisable app badge or pseudo-product logo. Never render real trademarked financial index names, ticker symbols, or financial product branding (for example S&P 500, NASDAQ, or Dow); use generic, unlabeled, non-readable charting visuals instead.

For any screen or device display that is semantically necessary to this hobby: the screen's content must be abstract, non-readable, non-branded light, color, or texture - never a readable UI, never a wall of code, never a fake dashboard (unless the hobby's identity genuinely requires a dashboard-like readout, in which case keep any numbers/labels abstract and non-legible), and never a human portrait, face thumbnail, social-media profile photo, or video-call participant of any kind, on any screen or poster anywhere in the scene. The screen should visually support the object or system already established as this card's protagonist, never introduce a human subject of its own. Where a screen is not essential to communicating this hobby, avoid a front-facing screen entirely and prefer physical equipment, process, or environment instead.

This artwork must contain ZERO real human presence - no people, no faces, no heads, no hands, no arms, no legs, no feet, no body parts, no human silhouettes, no crowds, no spectators, no players, no workers, no staff, no passersby, no portraits, no photographs of people, no screen images of people, no posters containing people, no reflections containing people, no person-shaped shadows, no cropped humans, and no distant background humans. This rule applies BOTH to the physical scene AND to any media, screen, or display shown inside the scene. Hobby-intrinsic non-real human-LIKE objects are allowed only when unmistakably small physical game pieces with a visible base/stand (tabletop miniatures, chess pieces, figurines) - never a dynamically-posed character with expressive facial detail. Real animals are allowed and encouraged where semantically appropriate (this is a zero-HUMANS rule, not a zero-living-beings rule). STRUCTURAL CONTAINMENT METHOD: do not design a normal human-centered scene and then try to remove the person - design the scene from the start so no human presence is structurally expected, per the matched structural_containment_rules_v2.json rule for this hobby's archetype. When a human is excluded from this scene, do NOT fill that human's role with a substitute character - no anthropomorphic animals, no mascots, no humanoid robots pretending to be a person, no toy or doll figures acting as full-scale scene participants, and no fantasy creatures performing a human professional or social role (for example, no owl acting as a lawyer or judge, no animal mascot standing in for a courtroom participant). The correct solution is an empty, structurally non-human scene, not a costumed stand-in. This rule does not apply to: a real animal where the animal itself is the genuine subject of the hobby (a zero-HUMANS rule, not a zero-living-beings rule); tabletop miniatures, chess pieces, or figurines that clearly read as small physical objects at miniature scale; statues or figurines that clearly read as objects, not living participants; media/collectible figures (for example anime-culture collectibles) that clearly read as small physical display objects; or a hobby that is specifically and literally about robots, where a robot is the genuine subject rather than a stand-in for a person.

Do not default to warm golden-hour light, a centered hero object, a cozy warm interior, or floating sparkle particles as the default treatment. Follow this card's assigned composition_diversity_v2.json routes (composition_archetype, palette_lighting_route, effect_level) exactly.

Do not solve a zero-human scene using invisible-human physics. Never show a tool, instrument, vessel, or object operating, pouring, swinging, or moving entirely on its own with no plausible physical cause - this reads as an erased person, not as an object-first composition. For example, never depict a watering can pouring while floating unsupported in mid-air, a racket or bat swinging with no hand and no prior momentum shown, a musical instrument playing itself with keys/strings moving with no cause. Depict this activity: An anime production and collecting workspace is the hero of the scene, built entirely from non-human fictional subject matter: small collectible figurines of an original mecha, robot, fantasy creature, or stylized animal (never a human or human-shaped figure) displayed on a simple stand, animation cels or storyboard/key-frame sheets showing original mecha, creature, or spaceship designs fanned out, an animation light table glowing beneath them, and manga/anime-style art books with blank or unreadable covers. If a screen is visible, it shows only an original mecha, robot, creature, or abstract animation-style visual with no human figure and no pseudo-Japanese decorative lettering anywhere. No school uniforms, no cosplay, no youthful or human-like character imagery of any kind, no body-focused or suggestive framing, no bedroom poster-wall staging. This must immediately communicate anime and Japanese animation production/collecting culture, never a generic conference hall, a generic cinema, or an abstract aurora light show.

Overall scene structure: An outdoor space at night or dusk, cool-toned ambient/artificial light.

Use this composition: A bold diagonal line (light, edge, or object arrangement) creates dynamic tension instead of a centered symmetrical shot.

Use this lighting and palette: A single warm light source (lamp, spotlight, oven glow) isolated against a cooler or dark surrounding.

Effects guidance: A small, semantically-motivated effect only (steam for food, dust for a track/trail, water droplets for water sports, light glints on glass/metal) - never a magical sparkle unrelated to the hobby's real physics.

The problem is unwanted/generated nonsense text (fake titles, slogans, labels, UI copy), not text as a concept. Do not return to a blanket 'all text is forbidden' rule. Text-like marks, diagrams, or notation may appear naturally on books, packaging, posters, boards, or documents, but must always be abstract, blurred, or non-legible - unlabeled diagram blocks, decorative symbols, gestural non-word marks. Never render a complete readable word, sentence, slogan, title, or brand name.

The artwork itself must be full-bleed and edge-to-edge with no card frame, no card border, no rounded card shell, no rarity badge, no title panel, no stats box, no TCG layout, and no watermark - the application adds any card UI separately.
